subject: 'ID Column' gone in recent update, how to recreate or at least retrieve 'feature name'

messages.author: 1648576ac1e3af20
messages.subject: 'ID Column' gone in recent update, how to recreate or at least retrieve 'feature name'
parts:
Dear Altuna,
I devised a complicated workflow for parsing methylDiff objects (generated by read.feature.flank --> regionCounts --> unite --> calculateDiffMeth) which relied on the 'ID Column'.
Can annotate.WithFeature get it back for me ... or at least the feature's 'name' column (from the bed file read to 'read.feature.flank' ) which I could then append onto a corresponding methylDiff object?

Thanks in advance,
Ben Rodriguez

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] 'ID Column' gone in recent update, how to recreate or at least retrieve 'feature name'
parts:
Hi Ben,
I am not sure I understand the question, but I guess you are trying to get the original features read by read.feature.flank (this reads in feature+flank)? if that's the case why don't you use findOverlaps() between as(methylDiff.obj,"GRanges") and the features (features should be GRanges objects as well). This should return a matrix showing which methylDiff object overlaps with which the feature.


Best,
Altuna

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] 'ID Column' gone in recent update, how to recreate or at least retrieve 'feature name'
parts:
Hi Altuna,
In the previous versions, I used the 'ID column' as a nifty index for all kinds of parsing outside of R. The format was ChrN.start.stop.BedNameField. I could do this because I always fed features in a bed file format with a name field.

I followed your suggestion and obtained the original "BedNameField" via the following steps:
# query is diff object, subject is feature object
test_findOverlaps<-as.matrix(findOverlaps(as(new_prom.refseq.diff,"GRanges"),new_prom.refseq.obj@listData$new_prom.refseq,type="equal",select="all"))
# get subject ID matching the query
new_prom.refseq.obj@listData$new_prom.refseq@elementMetadata@listData$name[test_findOverlaps[,2]]
# get subject ID matching the query and return data frame
new_prom.refseq.diff.id<-data.frame(new_prom.refseq.obj@listData$new_prom.refseq@elementMetadata@listData$name[test_findOverlaps[,2]],check.names=FALSE,stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
# change column name prior to write out
colnames(new_prom.refseq.diff.id)<-c("new_prom.refseq.diff.id")

Working this out led me to discover something about the new unite function. If a feature object has more than one entry sharing identical chromosome, start, stop, coordinates , unite behaves unexpectedly at region level.
for instance, I discovered my mouse promoter file contained three entries with identical chrom,start,stop (I had taken previous steps to remove such redundancies) :
chr3 104666423  104668423 NM_001253702 229681 +
chr3 104666423  104668423 NM_009797 12340 -
chr3 104666423  104668423 NM_153091 229681 +
Notice two are on the positive strand, one is on the negative strand. In a promoter region comparison of two pooled biological replicates per condition [methylBase obtained by pool(unite()) ], methylKit produced 81 separate entries total for the (+) coordinates [n = 54] and (-) coordinates [n = 27] in the methylBase and methylDiff objects. Only two entries are produced after I removed one of the (+) strand promoters and added 1 bp to the (-) strand promoter coordinates.

Regards,
Ben

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] 'ID Column' gone in recent update, how to recreate or at least retrieve 'feature name'
parts:
Hi Ben,
Thanks for pointing this out. I would expect this from the new unite function, since it only merges on chr,start,end and strand. If there are duplicate coordinates, depending on the number of samples you will end up with more duplicates as you have observed. 

It was nifty for me as well to add the name column to the id and do a merge based on that, but id column really inflates the memory footprint of the object and makes things harder when you have a lot of samples to deal with.

My advice would be that the users should check if their annotations/regions of interest have duplicated coordinates, and remove the ones that are duplicated. This is easy to do in GenomicRanges. Assume "gr" contains the regions of interest/annotations. The following removes the duplicated coordinates.

gr=gr[!duplicated(gr),]

Best,
Altuna
